clue.text: A fen, mist having moved, clear

indicators.note: letters that have moved no longer sit in their printed order, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Fog drifting off a marsh leaves the view clear.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the answer means plain to see or obvious, which is what clear means here.

clue.text: Island created fresh air

indicators.note: something made fresh is made anew, so the word after it is remade in a new order

blocks.note: a synonym of created
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An island boasts that it has invented fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, famous for its fortified wine.

clue.text: Older relative — of a kid?

blocks.note: surface reading: a grandmother, the older relative of a child
setter's reading: a kid is a young goat, whose mother is a female goat

explanation.walkthrough: The word is a familiar name for a grandmother and also the term for a female goat, the mother of a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an elderly family member of a child, and a female goat is the parent of a young goat.

clue.text: Witness insect awaiting swatter?

blocks.note: first meaning: an unnoticed observer of events
second meaning, taken literally: a fly resting on a vertical surface, an easy target

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom describes someone who watches without being noticed; read literally it is a fly sitting on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a silent unseen observer, someone present at events who goes unnoticed, which is a kind of witness.

clue.text: Tube where growths come up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: warts are small skin growths

explanation.surface: A pipe where some kind of growth is sprouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking straw is a thin hollow tube for sucking liquid up from a glass.

clue.text: Switch hands, passing to the left

indicators.note: in an across clue, moving leftwards means reading from right to left

blocks.note: paws is an informal word for hands

explanation.surface: An instruction in a card game or dance to change hands and pass something leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, which is one sense of switch as a verb.

clue.text: Thingummyjig has twit discombobulated

indicators.note: discombobulated means confused or thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Some unnamed gadget has left a fool baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal placeholder words for an object whose proper name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Ridiculous place to sit when training?

blocks.note: first meaning: crazy or foolish, in informal British usage
second meaning: the small chamber pot a toddler uses during toilet training

explanation.walkthrough: Training suggests sport or the gym, but it is toilet training for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the adjective means silly or mad, and the noun is a child's chamber pot used in toilet training.

clue.text: Arcade nearly collapsing — its days may be numbered

indicators.note: something collapsing falls apart, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A rundown shopping arcade is on the verge of falling down, its future short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like a deletion signal for arcade, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Each day in a twelve-month span from January to December has its own number, so its days are literally numbered.

clue.text: Not entirely good, and yet excellent!

indicators.note: the answer uses only part of the following words, sitting within them

blocks.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: Something is not wholly good, yet still praised as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandy is an informal, slightly old-fashioned adjective meaning very good or first-rate.

clue.text: Again change a physical exercise after study

indicators.note: placing one piece after another fixes the order in which the two parts join

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
taken as written
PT is physical training, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Someone revises a gym routine after doing some research.
explanation.definitionFit: To readapt is to adjust or modify once more, so it means alter a second time.

clue.text: Very cold part of anticyclone

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is used, lying within it

blocks.note: found inside this word

explanation.surface: A weather report notes bitter cold in one area of high pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy describes something freezing, as cold as ice, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Garment I’ve just bought in US state

blocks.note: something just bought is new
a jersey is a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: A tourist shows off a top they have just bought on a trip to America.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty states, on the east coast between New York and Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Settle a match

blocks.note: first meaning: to come down and rest, as a bird does on a branch
second meaning: what a struck match is, on fire

explanation.walkthrough: Settle a match sounds like deciding a sporting contest; a struck match is on fire, and a bird coming to rest lands.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means land or descend and perch; as an adjective it means burning, which describes a lit match.

clue.text: Middle Eastern serial I translated

indicators.note: translating changes words into a new form, so the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone has translated a television serial from a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Israeli means relating to Israel, a nation in the Middle East, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Journalist taking part in foxtrot I decided to knock over

indicators.note: the answer takes up only a section of the following words
knocking something over turns it end to end, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: A reporter joins a ballroom dance and then decides to bring a partner down.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a newspaper person who prepares copy for print, one kind of journalist.

clue.text: Badge pinned by maestro, setter

indicators.note: something pinned is held fast inside, so the answer is enclosed within the following words

blocks.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: A conductor and a crossword compiler pin on a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon formed into a circular decoration, worn as an emblem or prize.

clue.text: Whiskey trier and a few when drunk

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: the first part of the fodder
the second part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A taster samples some whiskey and has a few too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is a humorous informal term for strong spirits such as whiskey.

clue.text: Scrap of confetti flying high, iridescent ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the end, so each word contributes its final letter

blocks.note: the closing letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A shimmering scrap of confetti floats high in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap of confetti' reads as a small piece of paper, but 'of' starts the fodder and scrap is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informal for a scuffle or brawl, so it is a synonym for a punch-up.

clue.text: Dance in bronze and green light?

blocks.note: a bronze skin colour is a tan
a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: A dance performed in bronze costumes under green lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina, famous for its dramatic steps.

clue.text: Vehicle kaput, rear end knocked off

indicators.note: the rear end being knocked off means the final letter is removed

blocks.note: bust is slang for broken or kaput

explanation.surface: A broken-down vehicle has had its back smashed off.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers along a fixed route.

clue.text: Directors evidently yawning out loud?

indicators.note: saying something out loud means the answer matches how the word is spoken, not written

blocks.note: someone visibly yawning is plainly uninterested

explanation.surface: The company bosses are plainly stifling yawns in a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's directors sit together as the governing body, collectively called its board.

clue.text: Men and girl out for troll?

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the first part of the fodder
the second part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A group of men and a girl go out hunting a troll.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is a mischievous imaginary goblin, a folklore creature similar to a troll.

clue.text: Correct tax code extremely unusual

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters
unusual means out of the normal pattern, so the letters take an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A complaint that the correct tax code is extremely unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise and accurate, a synonym for correct as an adjective.

clue.text: Suddenly see part of a tree!

blocks.note: first meaning: informal British for suddenly realise or understand
second meaning: a small thin branch

explanation.walkthrough: To twig is British slang for catching on to something.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is informal for grasping a point in a flash, and the noun is a slender shoot growing from a branch.

clue.text: Scottish dish tasted by convict?

blocks.note: first meaning: oatmeal boiled in water or milk, traditional in Scotland
second meaning: British slang for time served in prison

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word means a prison sentence, so a convict experiences it; 'tasted' plays on the breakfast sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats boiled into a hot cereal are a Scottish staple, and doing time in jail is British slang for the same word.
